# Case 31: Hypothesis Testing H5a-H5d

## Introduction

This analysis examines factors influencing members' overall attitudes toward the managerial and operational efficiency of Employees Federal Credit Union (EFCU).

The analysis focuses on four hypotheses, H5a through H5d, concerning confidentiality, loan processing promptness, adequacy of financial services, and simplicity of loan applications.

A multiple linear regression analysis is used to determine whether these four factors significantly predict members' overall evaluations of the credit union.

# Research Objectives

## Purpose of the Analysis

The primary objective is to identify factors associated with members' overall attitudes toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

The four hypotheses examine:

- H5a: Confidentiality of personal financial information.
- H5b: Promptness of loan application processing.
- H5c: Adequacy of financial services in meeting members' needs.
- H5d: Simplicity and ease of loan applications.

All four hypotheses share the same dependent variable, making multiple regression an appropriate statistical method.

# Data Preparation

## Loading Required Packages

The analysis uses R to import, prepare, and analyze the SPSS survey dataset.

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(haven)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)
```

## Importing the Dataset

The cleaned SPSS dataset contains survey responses collected from members of Employees Federal Credit Union.

```{r}
#| label: import-data

efcu <- read_sav("Case 31 Data_efcu_4.sav")

# Display dataset dimensions
dim(efcu)

# Display variable names
names(efcu)

# Preview dataset
head(efcu)
```

## Identifying the Variables

The dependent variable is the overall managerial and operational efficiency rating.

The independent variables represent four specific aspects of the credit union's operations.

| Variable | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Q37_r | Dependent | Overall operational efficiency |
| Q31 | Independent | Confidentiality of financial information |
| Q32 | Independent | Loan application processing promptness |
| Q33 | Independent | Adequacy of financial services |
| Q34 | Independent | Simplicity of loan applications |

The dependent variable Q37_r is the recoded version of the overall management and operations rating.

## Preparing the Regression Data

The five variables are selected and converted to numeric values for regression analysis.

Only valid responses are retained. Responses outside the valid five-point scales and missing observations are excluded.

```{r}

#| label: prepare-data

# Display available variable names
names(efcu)

# Standardize variable names to uppercase
names(efcu) <- toupper(names(efcu))

# Create Q37_R if it does not exist
if (!"Q37_R" %in% names(efcu)) {

  if (!"Q37" %in% names(efcu)) {
    stop("Neither Q37_R nor Q37 exists in the dataset.")
  }

  # Reverse Q37 so higher values indicate
  # more favorable operational evaluations.
  # Original: 1 = Excellent, 5 = Very Poor
  # Reversed: 5 = Excellent, 1 = Very Poor
  efcu$Q37_R <- ifelse(
    as.numeric(efcu$Q37) %in% 1:5,
    6 - as.numeric(efcu$Q37),
    NA_real_
  )
}

# Select required variables
required_vars <- c(
  "Q37_R", "Q31", "Q32", "Q33", "Q34"
)

# Identify missing variables
missing_vars <- setdiff(
  required_vars,
  names(efcu)
)

if (length(missing_vars) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Missing variables: ",
    paste(missing_vars, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

# Prepare regression dataset
regression_data <- efcu |>
  dplyr::select(dplyr::all_of(required_vars)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::everything(),
      ~ as.numeric(.x)
    )
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    dplyr::across(
      dplyr::everything(),
      ~ ifelse(.x %in% 1:5, .x, NA_real_)
    )
  ) |>
  tidyr::drop_na()

# Rename dependent variable for consistency
names(regression_data)[
  names(regression_data) == "Q37_R"
] <- "Q37_r"

# Display results
summary(regression_data)
nrow(regression_data)

```

## Sample Characteristics

The original dataset contains `r nrow(efcu)` observations.

After excluding missing and invalid responses for the five regression variables, the final analysis includes `r nrow(regression_data)` complete observations.

Using complete cases ensures that the same respondents are included when estimating the effects of all four independent variables.

# Hypothesis Development

## H5a: Confidentiality of Financial Information

**Hypothesis H5a:**

Member belief that the credit union keeps personal financial information confidential will positively influence the overall attitude toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

- Independent variable: Q31
- Dependent variable: Q37_r

Members who believe their personal financial information is protected are expected to evaluate the credit union's operational efficiency more favorably.

## H5b: Loan Processing Promptness

**Hypothesis H5b:**

Loan application processing promptness will positively influence the overall attitude toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

- Independent variable: Q32
- Dependent variable: Q37_r

Members who believe loan applications are processed promptly are expected to report more favorable attitudes toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

## H5c: Adequacy of Financial Services

**Hypothesis H5c:**

Member satisfaction with the level of financial services in meeting their needs will positively influence the overall attitude toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

- Independent variable: Q33
- Dependent variable: Q37_r

Members who believe the credit union's services meet their financial needs are expected to evaluate its overall operations more favorably.

## H5d: Simplicity of Loan Applications

**Hypothesis H5d:**

Loan application simplicity and easiness will positively influence the overall attitude toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

- Independent variable: Q34
- Dependent variable: Q37_r

Members who consider loan applications simple and easy to complete are expected to have more favorable overall attitudes toward the credit union's operational efficiency.

# Multiple Regression Analysis

## Statistical Method

Multiple linear regression is used because the four hypotheses involve different independent variables but share one dependent variable.

The regression equation is:

$$
Q37_r = \beta_0 + \beta_1Q31 +
\beta_2Q32 + \beta_3Q33 +
\beta_4Q34 + \epsilon
$$

The analysis evaluates the independent contribution of each predictor while controlling for the other three predictors.

The significance level is set at alpha = 0.05.

## Running the Multiple Regression

```{r}
#| label: regression-model

model_h5 <- lm(
  Q37_r ~ Q31 + Q32 + Q33 + Q34,
  data = regression_data
)

# Regression summary
summary(model_h5)

# 95% confidence intervals
confint(model_h5)
```

## Extracting Regression Statistics

The following code extracts the regression coefficients, p-values, model fit statistics, and overall model significance.

```{r}
#| label: extract-results

model_summary <- summary(model_h5)

coefficients_table <- as.data.frame(
  model_summary$coefficients
)

coefficients_table$Variable <- rownames(
  coefficients_table
)

rownames(coefficients_table) <- NULL

names(coefficients_table) <- c(
  "Estimate",
  "Std_Error",
  "t_value",
  "p_value",
  "Variable"
)

r_squared <- model_summary$r.squared

adjusted_r_squared <-
  model_summary$adj.r.squared

f_statistic <- unname(
  model_summary$fstatistic[1]
)

df1 <- unname(
  model_summary$fstatistic[2]
)

df2 <- unname(
  model_summary$fstatistic[3]
)

model_p_value <- pf(
  f_statistic,
  df1,
  df2,
  lower.tail = FALSE
)

# Display model statistics
data.frame(
  R_Squared = r_squared,
  Adjusted_R_Squared = adjusted_r_squared,
  F_Statistic = f_statistic,
  Model_P_Value = model_p_value
) |>
  kable(digits = 4)
```

# Regression Results

## Overall Model Fit

The multiple regression model produced an R-squared value of **`r round(r_squared, 4)`** and an adjusted R-squared value of **`r round(adjusted_r_squared, 4)`**.

The four independent variables collectively explained approximately **`r round(r_squared * 100, 2)`%** of the variation in members' overall operational-efficiency ratings.

The overall regression F-statistic was **`r round(f_statistic, 3)`**, with a p-value of **`r format.pval(model_p_value, digits = 3)`**.

The overall regression model was **`r ifelse(model_p_value < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")`** at the 0.05 level.

These findings indicate whether the four operational factors collectively provide statistically significant explanatory power for members' overall evaluations.

## Regression Coefficients

```{r}
#| label: coefficient-table

coefficients_table |>
  select(
    Variable,
    Estimate,
    Std_Error,
    t_value,
    p_value
  ) |>
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Multiple Regression Coefficients"
  )
```

The coefficient estimates indicate the direction and magnitude of each relationship, holding the other predictors constant.

A p-value below 0.05 indicates that a coefficient differs significantly from zero.

Because higher values on the recoded Q37_r represent more favorable evaluations, and the agreement items are coded from strongly disagree to strongly agree, positive coefficients are consistent with the directions proposed in H5a through H5d.

# Individual Hypothesis Testing

## Preparing Hypothesis Decisions

```{r}
#| label: hypothesis-decisions

hypothesis_results <- coefficients_table |>
  filter(Variable != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(
    Hypothesis = case_when(
      Variable == "Q31" ~ "H5a",
      Variable == "Q32" ~ "H5b",
      Variable == "Q33" ~ "H5c",
      Variable == "Q34" ~ "H5d"
    ),
    Decision = ifelse(
      p_value < 0.05,
      "Reject H0",
      "Fail to reject H0"
    ),
    Support = ifelse(
      p_value < 0.05 & Estimate > 0,
      "Supported",
      "Not supported"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(Hypothesis)

hypothesis_results |>
  select(
    Hypothesis,
    Variable,
    Estimate,
    p_value,
    Decision,
    Support
  ) |>
  kable(
    digits = 4,
    caption = "Hypothesis Testing Results"
  )
```

## H5a: Confidentiality of Financial Information

The regression coefficient for confidentiality of personal financial information (Q31) was **`r round(coef(model_h5)["Q31"], 4)`**.

The p-value was **`r format.pval(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q31"], digits = 3)`**.

The relationship was **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q31"] < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")`** at the 0.05 level.

**Hypothesis Decision:**

H5a was **`r hypothesis_results$Support[hypothesis_results$Hypothesis == "H5a"]`**.

The results indicate that confidentiality of personal financial information **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q31"] < 0.05 & coef(model_h5)["Q31"] > 0, "has a statistically significant positive relationship with", "does not demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship with")`** members' overall attitudes toward operational efficiency, after controlling for the other predictors.

## H5b: Loan Application Processing Promptness

The regression coefficient for loan application processing promptness (Q32) was **`r round(coef(model_h5)["Q32"], 4)`**.

The p-value was **`r format.pval(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q32"], digits = 3)`**.

The relationship was **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q32"] < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")`** at the 0.05 level.

**Hypothesis Decision:**

H5b was **`r hypothesis_results$Support[hypothesis_results$Hypothesis == "H5b"]`**.

The results indicate that loan processing promptness **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q32"] < 0.05 & coef(model_h5)["Q32"] > 0, "has a statistically significant positive relationship with", "does not demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship with")`** members' overall attitudes toward operational efficiency, after controlling for the other predictors.

## H5c: Adequacy of Financial Services

The regression coefficient for adequacy of financial services (Q33) was **`r round(coef(model_h5)["Q33"], 4)`**.

The p-value was **`r format.pval(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q33"], digits = 3)`**.

The relationship was **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q33"] < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")`** at the 0.05 level.

**Hypothesis Decision:**

H5c was **`r hypothesis_results$Support[hypothesis_results$Hypothesis == "H5c"]`**.

The results indicate that adequacy of financial services **`r ifelse(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q33"] < 0.05 & coef(model_h5)["Q33"] > 0, "has a statistically significant positive relationship with", "does not demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship with")`** members' overall attitudes toward operational efficiency, after controlling for the other predictors.

## H5d: Simplicity of Loan Applications

The regression coefficient for simplicity and ease of loan applications (Q34) was **`r round(coef(model_h5)["Q34"], 4)`**.

The p-value was **`r format.pval(coefficients_table$p_value[coefficients_table$Variable == "Q34"], digits = 3)`**.

# Regression Diagnostics

## Checking Model Assumptions

Regression diagnostics are performed to evaluate the suitability of the multiple regression model.

The analysis examines:

- Linearity of the relationships.
- Approximately constant residual variance.
- Normality of residuals.
- Potential influential observations.
- Multicollinearity among predictors.

```{r}
#| label: diagnostic-plots
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 6

par(mfrow = c(2, 2))

plot(model_h5)

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

## Multicollinearity Assessment

Variance inflation factors (VIF) are calculated to evaluate multicollinearity among the four independent variables.

Higher VIF values indicate stronger linear relationships among predictors, which can make coefficient estimates less precise.

```{r}
#| label: vif-analysis

predictor_names <- c(
  "Q31", "Q32", "Q33", "Q34"
)

vif_values <- sapply(
  predictor_names,
  function(variable) {
    other_variables <- setdiff(
      predictor_names,
      variable
    )

    auxiliary_model <- lm(
      reformulate(
        other_variables,
        response = variable
      ),
      data = regression_data
    )

    1 / (1 - summary(auxiliary_model)$r.squared)
  }
)

data.frame(
  Predictor = names(vif_values),
  VIF = as.numeric(vif_values)
) |>
  kable(
    digits = 3,
    caption = "Variance Inflation Factors"
  )
```

## Diagnostic Findings

The regression diagnostic plots provide information about the residual distribution, variance consistency, and potentially influential observations.

The highest calculated variance inflation factor was **`r round(max(vif_values), 3)`**.

The VIF results **`r ifelse(max(vif_values) < 5, "do not indicate substantial multicollinearity using a threshold of 5", "indicate that multicollinearity warrants further investigation using a threshold of 5")`**.

The residual plots should also be reviewed visually before drawing final conclusions about the model assumptions.

## Interpretation of Findings

The multiple regression analysis examined four potential predictors of members' overall attitudes toward the operational efficiency of Employees Federal Credit Union.

Of the four hypotheses, **`r sum(hypothesis_results$Support == "Supported")`** received statistical support.

The model explained **`r round(r_squared * 100, 2)`%** of the variance in overall operational-efficiency ratings.

The findings help identify which aspects of the credit union's services are positively associated with members' overall evaluations when the other operational factors are held constant.

# Managerial Implications

## Implications for Employees Federal Credit Union

The regression findings can assist management in identifying operational areas associated with member satisfaction.

Confidentiality, loan processing promptness, adequacy of financial services, and simplicity of loan applications represent important aspects of the member experience.

Management should pay particular attention to factors showing statistically significant positive relationships with overall operational efficiency.

These findings can guide service evaluations and help prioritize operational improvements.

## Recommendations

Employees Federal Credit Union should use the regression findings to evaluate its operational practices.

Recommended actions include:

1. Continue protecting members' confidential financial information.
2. Monitor and improve loan application processing times.
3. Evaluate whether existing financial services adequately meet members' needs.
4. Simplify loan application procedures where possible.
5. Continue collecting member feedback to monitor operational performance.

The regression results identify associations and should not be interpreted as proof that changing a particular factor will cause an improvement in overall ratings.

# Conclusion

## Overall Conclusion

This analysis tested H5a through H5d using one multiple linear regression model.

The dependent variable was overall managerial and operational efficiency (Q37_r).

The independent variables were confidentiality (Q31), loan processing promptness (Q32), adequacy of financial services (Q33), and loan application simplicity (Q34).

The overall regression model was **`r ifelse(model_p_value < 0.05, "statistically significant", "not statistically significant")`**.

The analysis found that **`r sum(hypothesis_results$Support == "Supported")` out of four hypotheses** were supported.

These findings provide evidence about the relationships between members' perceptions of specific operational practices and their overall evaluation of Employees Federal Credit Union.
